tests.scope: Full suite after final production geometry/material source changes. Subsequent validation-harness correction only adds the required palette dry-run, with a complete real MCP rerun.

reviewed: All 12 front and material images through saved contact sheets, with rabbit, ornamental fish and pig inspected individually.
All 12 final MCP underside images through a newly regenerated contact sheet.
All four fauna-scale-study views, including isometric, front, back and material overview.
Actual rebuilt fish-folded, goose-relaxed and deer-narrow parameter screenshots.
findings: Species silhouettes remain distinct, with continuous faceted surfaces, curved necks, horns, tails, fins and feather shapes, plus small native voxel details.
No obvious floating eyes, ear interiors, legs or squirrel nose remain in the inspected views; actual triangle contact checks supply the separate geometric evidence.
Underside views show separated feet, split hooves, webbed feet and connected fin roots. Thin clefts are verified by coordinate checks in addition to screenshots.
The metre-scale isometric scene shows relative author sizes. Front and back views overlap rows in projection; individual screenshots provide unobstructed per-asset inspection.
Geometric coat patterns, small projecting eyes and block-like smallest claws remain stylized and require human art review.
visualReview.scope: Assistant visual inspection only; no claim of original runtime dimensions, biological motion, habitat placement, physical support or human art acceptance.

limitations: All technical candidates; human art acceptance zero.
Original species dimensions, runtime animal contracts and source skeletons unavailable.
One prop root per animal; no quadruped/bird/fish rig, gait, flight, swimming, soft skin or fur.
All visual meshes noncollision. Triangle/contact checks do not establish physical support or biomechanical correctness.
Finite static forms only, including held nut with no resource or inventory generation.
Independent viewport fitting is not a common metre scale; saved scene provides metre-scale display only.
Faceted eyes, beaks, hoof/toe details and geometric coat patterns remain for human art review.
Software WebGL does not certify hardware frame rates.
